title: Estado Novo Authoritarian Rule Under Salazar
note: Salazar regime, PIDE secret police, economic underdevelopment all confirmed for 1950.

title: Salazar Reclassifies Colonies as 'Overseas Provinces'
note: 1951 constitutional revision reclassifying colonies as overseas provinces confirmed.

title: Portugal Joins the United Nations
note: Portugal admitted 14 December 1955 in a package deal of 16 new members. Confirmed.

title: Emigration Wave to France and Western Europe Begins
note: Emigration to France accelerated from late 1950s; remittances confirmed. Year plausible as start.

title: Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation Established in Lisbon
note: Foundation was established on 18 July 1956, not 1957. Year off by 1.

title: General Humberto Delgado's Defiant Presidential Campaign
note: Election held 8 June 1958; Delgado's 'obviously I'll fire him' quote confirmed.

title: Pidjiguiti Massacre in Guinea-Bissau
note: Massacre occurred on 3 August 1959, not 1960. Year off by 1.

title: Angola War of Independence Begins
note: War began 1961 with multiple uprisings. FNLA formally named March 1962 but uprising started 1961. Verified.

title: India Annexes Goa — Humiliating Loss for Estado Novo
note: Operation Vijay December 1961; 36-hour operation confirmed; 450+ years of Portuguese rule confirmed.

title: Academic Crisis — Students Protest Dictatorship
note: Academic Crisis of 1962 at Lisbon and Coimbra confirmed; PIDE arrests confirmed.

title: Military Conscription Dramatically Expanded for Colonial Wars
note: Conscription expansion confirmed; army grew to 217,000 by 1974. Over 200,000 figure is accurate for later in the war.

title: Mozambique War of Independence Opens
note: FRELIMO's first attack 25 September 1964 in Cabo Delgado confirmed.

title: Salazar Bridge (Ponte 25 de Abril) Opens Over Tagus
note: Inaugurated 6 August 1966; longest suspension bridge in Europe at the time; renamed confirmed.

title: General Delgado Assassinated by PIDE in Spain
note: Delgado was assassinated on 13 February 1965, not 1966. Year off by 1.

title: Salazar Incapacitated — Caetano Becomes Prime Minister
note: Salazar stroke September 1968; Caetano appointed 27 September 1968 confirmed.

title: Death of Salazar — End of an Era
note: Salazar died 27 July 1970, age 81; never told he had been removed confirmed.

title: Armed Forces Movement Forms Among Disillusioned Officers
note: MFA was formally founded 9 September 1973, not 1970. Event describes clandestine discussion groups forming in ~1970, which is a precursor phase only; the organization itself formed in 1973. Title is misleading for this year.

title: MFA Formally Organized — Coup Planning Begins
note: MFA formally founded 9 September 1973 confirmed.

title: PAIGC Declares Guinea-Bissau Independence
note: Independence declared 24 September 1973; Cabral assassinated 20 January 1973 confirmed.

title: Carnation Revolution — April 25 Ends Dictatorship
note: All key facts confirmed: April 25 1974, MFA coup, Grandola Vila Morena, carnations in rifle barrels.

title: PIDE Secret Police Dissolved After Coup
note: DGS (formerly PIDE) dissolved after April 25 1974 coup confirmed.

title: Revolutionary Turmoil — Hot Summer of 1975
note: Hot Summer of 1975, factory occupations, left-right struggle for power all confirmed.

title: Angola and Mozambique Independence — Chaotic Decolonization
note: Mozambique independent 25 June 1975; Angola 11 November 1975. Dates confirmed.

title: Retornados — 500,000–800,000 Settlers Return from Africa
note: Estimates 500,000 to 1 million; range in event (500k-800k) consistent with sources.

title: Constitution of 1976 Adopted — Democratic Republic Established
note: Constitution adopted 2 April 1976 confirmed.

title: First Free Parliamentary Elections — Mário Soares PM
note: First free elections April 1976; Soares as PM, Eanes as president confirmed.

title: Portugal Applies for EEC Membership
note: Formal application submitted 28 March 1977 by Soares confirmed.

title: First IMF Stabilization Program
note: Portugal drew first tranche in 1977; formal standby arrangement concluded May 1978. Event year of 1977 is when discussions and first drawing occurred.

title: Prime Minister Sá Carneiro Killed in Plane Crash
note: Died in plane crash 4 December 1980. Circumstances disputed (accident vs bomb). Facts confirmed.

title: Council of Revolution Abolished — Military Removed from Politics
note: Council of Revolution disbanded 30 September 1982 by first constitutional revision; Constitutional Court created.

title: Second IMF Program — Fiscal Stabilization Before EEC
note: Second IMF program confirmed in 1983.

title: Cavaco Silva Takes PSD Leadership — Reform Agenda
note: Cavaco Silva became PSD leader and PM in 1985 confirmed.

title: Portugal Joins the European Economic Community
note: Portugal and Spain joined EEC 1 January 1986 confirmed.

title: Mário Soares Elected President — First Civilian Since Estado Novo
note: Soares elected president February 1986; first civilian in 60 years confirmed.

title: Cavaco Silva Wins Unprecedented Absolute Majority
note: PSD won 50.2% and 148 seats; first absolute majority in democratic era confirmed.

title: Chiado Fire Destroys Historic Lisbon Quarter
note: Fire on 25 August 1988; Álvaro Siza Vieira reconstruction confirmed.

title: EU Single Market Completed — Full Integration for Portugal
note: Single market completed end of 1992 confirmed.

title: Lisbon Named European Capital of Culture
note: Lisbon was European Capital of Culture 1994 confirmed.

title: António Guterres Becomes Prime Minister
note: Guterres won October 1995 elections; became PM 28 October 1995 confirmed.

title: Community of Portuguese Language Countries (CPLP) Founded
note: East Timor listed as a founding member is materially wrong — East Timor joined in 2002. The seven founders were Angola, Brazil, Cape Verde, Guinea-Bissau, Mozambique, Portugal, São Tomé and Príncipe.

title: Vasco da Gama Bridge Opens — Longest in Europe
note: Bridge was inaugurated on 29 March 1998, not 1997. Year off by 1.

title: Expo 98 World's Fair Draws 11 Million to Lisbon
note: Official visitor count was 10,128,204 (just over 10 million). Event states '11 million' — materially wrong.

title: José Saramago Wins Nobel Prize in Literature
note: Nobel Prize in Literature 1998 confirmed; first Portuguese-language writer from Portugal confirmed.

title: Portugal Joins the Euro as Founding Member
note: Portugal one of 11 founding eurozone members 1 January 1999 confirmed.

title: East Timor Votes for Independence — Portugal's Diplomatic Win
note: Referendum 30 August 1999; 78.5% voted for independence; Australian-led INTERFET confirmed.

title: Drug Decriminalization Model Draws Global Attention
note: Decriminalization came into effect July 2001 confirmed; global attention confirmed.

title: Azores Summit Hosts Bush, Blair, Aznar — Iraq War
note: Summit 16 March 2003 at Lajes; Barroso as host PM confirmed.

title: Catastrophic Forest Fires Burn 430,000 Hectares
note: Hectares (~425,000–471,000 range in sources) broadly consistent. Deaths: sources report 18 killed, not 'at least 21' as stated. Death toll materially wrong but hectares approximately right. Borderline — marking UNVERIFIED.

title: UEFA Euro 2004 Hosted in Portugal
note: Portugal hosted Euro 2004; Greece defeated Portugal 1-0 in the final confirmed.

title: Sócrates Government Launches Technological Modernization Plan
note: Sócrates won February 2005 with absolute majority; Technological Plan launched confirmed.

title: Lisbon Treaty Signed at EU Summit
note: Signed 13 December 2007 in Lisbon; entered into force 1 December 2009 confirmed.

title: Budget Deficit Surges to 10% of GDP — Crisis Deepens
note: Deficit ~9.4–10% of GDP in 2009 confirmed; Excessive Deficit Procedure confirmed.

title: Geração à Rasca Mass Protest — Generation in a Bind
note: 12 March 2011 protest; ~300,000–500,000 people; largest since Carnation Revolution confirmed.

title: EU/IMF Troika Bailout — €78 Billion Package
note: €78 billion bailout, April 2011 request, Sócrates resignation confirmed.

title: 'Que se Lixe a Troika' — Massive Anti-Austerity Protests
note: 15 September 2012 protest; 500,000–1 million; government retreated on social security contribution hike confirmed.

title: Unemployment Peaks at 17.5% — Mass Emigration Wave
note: Unemployment peaked ~17.5% in 2013; youth unemployment ~38%; emigration wave confirmed.

title: Portugal Exits EU/IMF Bailout Without Precautionary Credit
note: Portugal exited bailout May 2014 without precautionary credit line confirmed.

title: Geringonça Left Coalition — Costa PM Without Majority
note: October 2015 election; geringonça minority government with Left Bloc and Communists confirmed.

title: Pedrogão Grande Wildfires Kill 66 — Worst in Portuguese History
note: 17-18 June 2017; 66 deaths confirmed as official count; eucalyptus monoculture debate confirmed.

title: Web Summit Moves to Lisbon — Tech Hub Status Emerges
note: Web Summit moved from Dublin to Lisbon in 2016, not 2017. Year off by 1.

title: Costa Wins Absolute Majority — Economy Near Full Employment
note: Costa did NOT win an absolute majority. PS won 108 of 230 seats (36.7%); it was a plurality, not majority. Title and description claim 'absolute majority' and 'without formal left-wing support' — both materially wrong.

title: COVID-19 — First State of Emergency Since 1974 Revolution
note: State of emergency declared 18 March 2020; first since 1974 Carnation Revolution confirmed.

title: Tourism Collapse — GDP Contracts 8.4%
note: GDP contracted 8.4% in real terms in 2020 confirmed by Statistics Portugal.

title: Fastest COVID-19 Vaccination in Europe — Army-Led Campaign
note: 85% full vaccination by October 2021; Vice-Admiral Gouveia e Melo confirmed; world-leading rate confirmed.

title: Housing Affordability Crisis Intensifies in Lisbon and Porto
note: Housing prices surge in Lisbon/Porto driven by tourism, short-term rentals, golden visa confirmed.

title: Costa Resigns Amid Corruption Investigation
note: Costa resigned 7 November 2023 amid corruption probe on lithium/hydrogen contracts; elected European Council president confirmed.

title: Chega Far-Right Surges — Third-Largest Political Force
note: March 2024 elections; Chega won 18% and 50 seats; third-largest party confirmed.

title: Portugal Marks 50 Years Since Carnation Revolution
note: The 50th anniversary of the Carnation Revolution was celebrated on April 25, 2024, not 2025. Year off by 1 — the 51st anniversary would be in 2025, not the 50th.

title: Lithium Mining Controversy — Critical Minerals vs. Environment
note: Portugal's lithium reserves among largest in Europe; EU strategic interest; local environmental opposition all confirmed.
